https://tribune.com.pk/story/2621343/de-.text: Home Sports De Minaur beats teen Hewitt He advanced into the Washington Open quarter-finals Defending champion Alex de Minaur powered into the Washington Open quarter-finals with a clinical 6-2, 6-3 victory over fellow Australian Cruz Hewitt. Men's second seed Ben Shelton also advanced, as did women's top seed Jessica Pegula and No. 2 Elina Svitolina. Top-seeded De Minaur was always likely to prove too much for 17-year-old qualifier Hewitt -- son of Aussie great LleytonHewitt -- who had only captured his first ATP victory in Tuesday's first round. The first set threatened to become a demolition as De Minaurraced to a 5-0 lead. But Hewitt found his feet, breaking back in the sixth game and holding serve before succumbing 6-2. Cheered on by a crowd that included his famous father, Hewitt started the second set brightly. But he was broken again on his second service game and could not reel in De Minaur, who warmly embraced the youngster at the net after taking the match. It was the first head-to-head ATP Tour match between the two, who have known each other for years. "It was definitely weird," said De Minaur. "I knew I was going to play him on the tour someday, but I didn't actually expect it to be this week. "It was an amazing feeling. Even all the lead up, seeing all the incredible pictures that we have together and how we've both grown up. "I'm glad I managed to get through, but I'm sure we're going to have many battles in the years to come." De Minaur next faces American Brandon Nakashima, who upset Czech seventh seed Jakub Mensik 7-6 (7/5), 3-6, 6-4. US home hope Shelton advanced with a gritty 6-7 (3/7), 6-3, 6-4, victory over France's Ugo Humbert. After handing Humbert the first set with a double fault on set point, Shelton dominated the second. But the third set was a tense affair and after seizing a break for a 5-4 lead Shelton had to fend off a break point before polishing off the match with a sharply angled serve that Humbert smacked into the net. "For me, it was all about heart tonight," Shelton said after lining up a meeting with Chile's Alejandro Tabile, a 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) winner over France's Terence Atmane. Pegula also had to rally from a set down, saying she started her match against Poland's Frech "just a little off" after a first-round bye. "I wasn't quite attacking the ball, and I felt like once I did that, then everything else kind of started to click together," said Pegula, who finished with 42 winners and won 12 of the last 15 games to triumph 3-6, 6-3, 6-0. Pegula next plays fifth-seeded Anna Kalinskaya, who saved two match points to beat Indonesia's Janice Tjen 1-6, 6-3, 7-6 (9/7). Ukraine's Svitolina booked her quarter-final berth with a 7-6 (7/4), 6-4 victory over Uzbekistan's Polina Kudermetova. She'll face rising Philippines star Alexandra Eala for a place in the semi-finals. COMMENTS Comments are moderated and generally will be posted if they are on-topic and not abusive. Photograph: The Washington Post/Getty Images San Diego Padres San Diego Padres minor-league staffer detained by ICE after arrest in Texas Family says Venezuelan has pending asylum claim DHS says 34-year-old faces removal proceedings Guardian sport Tue 18 Aug 2026 14.00 EDT Last modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 14.03 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google San Diego Padres minor-league catching coordinator Oswaldo Pirela remained in federal immigration custody on Tuesday after being detained at an airport in El Paso, Texas, while returning from a work trip. Pirela’s family said the 34-year-old Venezuelan has a pending asylum claim and has continually renewed his work authorization. The Department of Homeland Security said he does not have legal status and will face removal proceedings. Pirela was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at El Paso International Airport early on Sunday, according to his relatives. His sister, Daniela Pirela, told NBC News that he was stopped at about 5am. His wife, Kemberly Avila, told The Athletic that he had been preparing to fly home to Arizona. Pirela had been working with the El Paso Chihuahuas, the Padres’ Triple-A affiliate. His family said he regularly travels for his role with the organization. “We recently became aware of the detainment of minor league catching coordinator Oswaldo Pirela in El Paso, Texas,” the Padres said in a statement. “We are working to gather additional information and will not have any further comment at this time.” Major League Baseball told CNN that the Padres had contacted Pirela’s family. Avila said the club was helping them and that she had spoken with her husband since his detention. According to ESPN, Pirela’s brother said he was not carrying his physical work-permit card when he was stopped. Avila told The Athletic that the family have pending asylum applications and carry temporary identification cards. Pirela arrived in the US from Venezuela and applied for asylum in 2014, his relatives said. They said he fled political persecution and has renewed his work authorization whenever it approached expiration. His family also said he is pursuing an EB-2 visa, an employment-based route to permanent residency. DHS disputed the family’s description of his immigration status. The department told CNN that Pirela entered the US illegally in 2014 and received permission to remain until February 2018. Officials said he stayed beyond that date and was not carrying documentation giving him legal status when he was approached. DHS said he would remain in ICE custody while removal proceedings continued. “Work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the United States,” a DHS spokesperson said. Pirela lives outside Phoenix with Avila and their two US-born daughters. Daniela Pirela told NBC News that she had spoken with him briefly but knew little about the conditions in which he was being held. She said her brother told her he was all right, although she believed he was trying to prevent the family from worrying. Pirela joined the Padres’ player-development staff in 2024. He previously spent three seasons as a catcher in the Texas Rangers’ minor-league system, playing in the Dominican Summer League from 2009 to 2011. His detention comes amid the Trump administration’s push to accelerate deportations and expand the range of immigrants subject to arrest. MLB has previously been pulled into the administration’s immigration crackdown. Last year the Los Angeles Dodgers said they refused ICE agents access to stadium parking areas during enforcement operations in the city. It was unclear on Tuesday when Pirela would next appear before an immigration court. https://www.politico.eu/article/iceland-.text: The future of Iceland’s bid to join the European Union will be called into question before its parliament after a majority of voters voted against restarting accession talks in this weekend’s referendum. A tally of votes on Sunday morning, reported by Iceland’s national broadcaster, RÚV, showed that Icelanders rejected the government’s bid to resume negotiations with the bloc, with 52.8 percent voting against and 47.2 percent in favor, amid an 82.5 percent turnout. “We will discuss with the parliamentary foreign affairs committee how best to close this chapter. We do not intend to make any firm decisions on that,” said Social Democratic Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir Sunday at a press conference when asked what the results meant for the future of Iceland’s bid. Advertisement Advertisement Frostadóttir reiterated, however, that the referendum outcome will be respected, that no further accession negotiations with the EU will be undertaken during the ruling government’s term, and that EU accessions were likely to be a theme of the next general elections. “It’s crucial right now that we take stock; we make a decision on what we do with … the application,” she said. The prime minister did not say when the matter would be put to parliament. Iceland first started talks to join the EU in 2009, talks which collapsed in 2013. The application, however, was never formally withdrawn. She also said that the result would not impact her role as prime minister because the referendum “was not a party political matter” — despite her support for restarting talks. Eiríkur Bergmann, a professor of politics at Bifröst University, called the vote a “heavy blow” for the government. “The coalition will emerge significantly weakened domestically, having staked considerable political capital on securing a mandate to reopen these negotiations,” he said. “However, the government will probably still survive the loss.” Advertisement Advertisement He added that the win for the “no” vote was largely due to a “highly technical” and “passionless campaign” that left voters to “ultimately prefer the safety of the status quo.” Sandro Gozi, a member of the European Parliament and secretary-general of the European Democratic Party, said that the result is a “warning” Europe should heed. “The EU’s power of attraction remains strong and undiminished, but it can never be taken for granted.” “The Commission respects the choice of the Icelandic people. Iceland remains a close partner of the European Union,” a Commission spokesperson said.

Photograph: Susan Greenwood/Hulton Archive/Getty Images Art theft Art dealer who sold forged Warhols sentenced to nearly four years in prison Leslie Roberts, 62, who created fraudulent invoices and authentication documents, also ordered to repay $2.6m Eric Berger Sat 17 Oct 2026 16.22 EDT Last modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 06.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Miami art dealer who admitted to selling forged Andy Warhol artwork has been sentenced to nearly four years in prison. Leslie Roberts, 62, created fraudulent invoices and authentication documents, as well as counterfeit stamps to deceive buyers, the US justice department said in a statement issued on Thursday. The US district judge Roy Altman sentenced Roberts to three years and 10 months in federal prison on 2 October. The Associated Press reported that Altman also ordered Roberts to repay $2.6m stolen through his scheme centering on artwork falsely attributed to the leader of the pop art movement. Roberts sold the fakes in question through his Miami art gallery, claiming he acquired the artwork from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, according to the justice department. He provided fraudulent invoices that appeared to have been issued by the organization before pleading guilty in June to conspiring to commit wire fraud. He also enlisted Carlos Rodriguez Melendez to pose as an employee of a New York-based auction company and falsely authenticate the work. The accomplice also pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. A statement from the southern district of Florida’s US attorney, Jason Reding Quiñones, said it was important to prosecute Roberts “because art fraud undermines confidence in the legitimate art market and victimizes buyers who rely on the authenticity of the works they purchase”. Roberts “exploited the trust that collectors place in art dealers and the authenticity of the works they purchase”, Reding Quiñones said. Reding Quiñones said Roberts’ prison sentence “sends a clear message: fraud is fraud, whether it happens on Wall Street or in an art gallery. Those who profit through deception will be held accountable.” Others have also been convicted in recent months of selling fake Warhol work. In April, a father and daughter in New Jersey, Erwin Bankowski and Karolina Bankowska, admitted to commissioning an artist in Poland to create at least 200 Warhol, Banksy and Pablo Picasso fakes and ultimately defrauding buyers of at least $2m. The pair pleaded guilty to running a years-long counterfeiting scheme in which they tricked galleries and auction houses into buying the forgeries. When sentenced, they could face up to 20 years’ imprisonment as well as at least $1.9m in restitution, the US justice department said in a statement.
